messages:
alex: thinking about an adaptive microburst algorithm that picks kernel based on runtime queue depth + KV hit ratio. want to validate before we flip. p95 SLO is 120ms. main tradeoff: bigger microbatches give throughput but can blow the tail.

chris: replays are good for fidelity but they hide some convoying artifacts if we don't preserve client-side jitter. propose: replay (orig timestamps), replay (normalized poisson), synthetic burst runs. compare.

mira: agree. also split warm vs cold KV in the matrix. KV churn changes kernel perf a lot. per-model thresholds > global. @alex can you add prefix-caching toggles? :+1:

sam: i can run microbatch sweep. suggest microbatch sizes [4,8,12,16,32]. last time we used threshold=12 for the kernel picker; should try lower for chatty tails.

jia: watch out for kernel flapping. if the picker switches kernels every few requests you'll pay copies and stalls -> p99 spikes. add a sticky window (e.g. 200-500ms) after a switch. also consider hysteresis: require sustained metric change for 2-3 samples.

perf-bot: starting run 4789: replay="may-traffic" mode=orig-ts infra=8xA100 model=gpt-like-8b duration=3600s. tags=[adaptive-kernel, microbatch-sweep]

perf-bot: partial summary (first 600s):
```
config: microbatch=8, sticky_ms=200, prefix_cache=enabled
samples: 64k
p50: 42ms  p95: 98ms  p99: 310ms
throughput: 210 req/s per GPU
kv_hit: 0.62  avg_seq_len: 74
notes: visible convoying during 2 windows at t=120s and t=410s
```

alex: hmm. p95 looks great but p99 310ms is rough. when i switch microbatch=16 (same sticky), perf-bot run shows p50:65ms p95:130ms p99:180ms and throughput up ~10%. so smaller microbatch helps p95 but amplifies tail noise here.

mira: leaning toward bounded tail over best p95. for product SLOs we want p99<200ms even if p95 is slightly higher. could we do hybrid: microbatch target 8 but cap concurrency per-actor and auto-upshift microbatch during sustained low-latency periods?

sam: also try adding a tiny randomized jitter on request start (2-8ms) to break convoys. synthetic load will show whether it's a deterministic convoy or emergent.

chris: propose final methodology for this experiment family: 1) replay original timestamps (fidelity) 2) replay normalized poisson (smooth) 3) synthetic stress with tail-only spikes (convoy stress). For each: warm and cold KV, microbatch sweep, sticky window sweep. Report p50/p95/p99, throughput, kv_hit, and a "tail-flatness" metric (p99/p95 ratio).

alex: good checklist. i'll schedule runs tomorrow and include the sticky window options [0,200,500]ms. experiment plan:
```
for mb in 4 8 12 16 32; do
  for sticky in 0 200 500; do
    loadgen --replay may-traffic --mb $mb --sticky $sticky --warm-kv yes --duration 3600
  done
done
```

jia: add a run with kernel-picker disabled (static kernel A and static kernel B) as ground truth. that helps quantify picker overhead.

perf-bot: queued 15 runs. expect results in ~18h. i'll post aggregated tables and CSVs once done.

alex: perfect. final note: make sure we log kernel-switch timestamps and memory/copy stalls. without those we won't know if picker overhead is main culprit.

mira: and add p95/p99 time-series (1s bins) so we can see transient spikes. easy to miss in aggregated metrics.

sam: ok i'll own the runs + initial postproc. thanks all. :rocket:
